note: Known failure modes, one row per entry of failure_modes/<tool>.yaml. Each quote was checked against its source by scripts/failure_modes.py --check.

entries.finding: For 32 proteins, pLDDT came from AlphaFold models of a different sequence version. The pile-up page now leaves pLDDT empty for those proteins, 196 regions in all.

evidence.quote: pLDDT came from AlphaFold models of a different sequence version for 32 proteins, and is now null there (196 regions without pLDDT).

entries.what_to_do: Check that a model's sequence equals the searched sequence before reading pLDDT from it.

entries.finding: In the ELM motif run, Foldseek was scored on orthologs that have no AlphaFold model. It cannot search those, so its share of motifs found is low for a reason that is not the search.
entries.number_note: The source does not count the orthologs with no AlphaFold model.

evidence.quote: Foldseek and Reseek were scored on orthologs with no AlphaFold model too, so their shares are low for a reason that is not the search

entries.what_to_do: Score a structure tool only on proteins that have a structure, and print how many proteins were left out.

entries.finding: A call is the whole alignment, not the target's domain placed on the query, so a long alignment over repeats never lands on one repeat. On a 23-aa LRR_1 repeat, every MMseqs2 and phmmer call was 47 aa or longer, so none landed.
entries.number: 47 aa or longer, on a 23-aa repeat

evidence.quote: But every one of their calls is 47 aa or longer, so under half of it lies inside a 23-aa repeat, and the landing rule (at least half the call inside the domain) rejects it.
a call is the whole alignment, not the target's domain projected onto the query, so long alignments over repeats never land on one repeat.
Olga's decision (2026-10-14, before the test half was read): a call is the target domain placed on the query through the hit, and MMseqs2 runs one round (2067fa1; recorded in nb 280's first cell).

entries.run: the time-split pilot's tune half (notebook 280), rapeseed protein A0A078HBQ0, LRR_1 repeats 64-86 and 88-110
entries.what_to_do: Place the target's domain on the query through the alignment before scoring. Notebook 280 switched to this rule.

entries.finding: Aligner calls start a median 5 to 21 residues before the domain, and cover 66–78% of the flank residues (the 100 residues either side of the domain), because a call spans the whole aligned stretch.
entries.number: median 5 to 21 residues early; 66–78% of flank residues

evidence.quote: Aligners start a median 5 to 21 residues early, because a call spans the whole aligned stretch.
**Flanks:** aligner calls cover 66–78% of flank residues, so their curves never fall to 0.2 within 100 residues.

entries.run: `make leaderboard-pileup` and the region pile-up page (Figures 3 and 4)
entries.what_to_do: Read a call's ends as the alignment's ends, not the domain's. To score where a domain sits, place the target's domain through the alignment.

entries.finding: HMMER rounds E-values to two significant figures. Counting E ≤ cutoff on those rounded values, instead of E < cutoff, made the dark-set counts 2 to 222 lower. The dark set is the proteins that no search tool hits below the cutoff.

evidence.quote: The pipeline's own dark set uses E ≤ cutoff, and HMMER rounds E-values to two significant figures. Under that rule the dark counts are 2 to 222 lower; Botryllus at E ≤ 10 is 2_039.

entries.run: notebook 289, dark set and kmerseek reach at E < 1 vs E < 10
entries.what_to_do: Say whether each cutoff is strict (E < 1) or not (E ≤ 1), and use the same rule in every count that is compared.

entries.finding: kmerseek 0.4.0 keys each index entry by its k-mer set, so two different sequences with the same k-mer set become one entry. In a regions-index pilot, 6 of 99_232 rows showed another sequence's residues. In an index of 125 ribonucleases, 31 are missing under cys2 and 7 under cys_hp3.

evidence.quote: In the 2024-kmerseek-analysis regions-index pilot (kmerseek v0.4.0, protein20, k=5), 6 of 99_232 rows had a `target_subseq` that is not `target[target_start:target_end]`.
Two different sequences with the same k-mer set get the same sum. So the second entry's hits came out with the first entry's coordinates and residues.
That is why 31 of the 125 ribonucleases are absent under `cys2` and 7 under `cys_hp3`.

entries.run: the regions-index pilot (kmerseek v0.4.0, protein20, k=5), and the 125 test ribonucleases searched with topi ribonuclease (P00659)
entries.what_to_do: Rebuild every 0.4.0 index once kmerseek PR 141 is merged; it keys each entry by its sequence. Until then, a recall number from a 0.4.0 index is measured against a reference that may be missing targets.

entries.finding: The exact Poisson score (`region_poisson_score`) stops at 307.65, where the p-value underflows. In 102 of 107 exact settings, decoy pairs reach that ceiling, so the decoy-matched cutoff sits above it and those settings find nothing.

evidence.quote: `region_poisson_score` stops at 307.65, which is -log10 of the smallest normal double: the Poisson p-value underflows. In 102 of 107 exact settings, at least two tune decoy-family pairs reach that ceiling. The matched cutoff then sits just above it, and those settings find nothing at all.
b215e87 scores the exact arm on `region_tfidf` (Olga, 2026-10-14; recorded in nb 280's first cell).

entries.run: the time-split pilot's tune half, 186 settings (notebook 280)
entries.what_to_do: Compute the p-value in log space inside kmerseek. Until then, score exact settings on `region_tfidf`, as notebook 280 now does.

entries.finding: Three rounds of profile search gave dipeptide-shuffled decoy proteins hits as strong as E 1e-22. One round gave them none below E 0.026. A cutoff set from decoys under three rounds is therefore set by the profile drifting toward a family, not by the search.

evidence.quote: The 3-round profile search gave dipeptide-shuffled decoys hits down to E 1e-22, and one round gives none below E 0.026.

entries.run: `make mmseqs-one-round`, Slurm job 47690191, on the time-split pilot's tune half; tables in `pilot_partial_2026-10-13/mmseqs_one_round/`
entries.what_to_do: Run one round (`--num-iterations 1`) when a cutoff is matched to decoys, or set the cutoff separately for each number of rounds.
